events.headline: Urda Rail Crash Probe Focuses on Signal-Override Order From Madrid Control Centre
events.summary: Investigators probing the Oct 28 high-speed rail collision near Urda (at least 68-69 killed) say that after a computer failure disabled the automatic safety system, an operator at Adif's Madrid-Atocha control centre told the AVE driver to resume normal running despite a red signal, even though the other train had reported it was still stopped on the track. Spain's rail accident authority has widened the investigation.

events.headline: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Tops 10,400 Cases With Case-Fatality Rate Above 50%, Spread Confirmed Abroad
events.summary: The outbreak, centered in Ituri Province, has reached 10,445 cumulative cases and 5,372 deaths in DRC, a case-fatality rate near 51-52%, making it the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in DRC history. Confirmed cases also reported in Kenya, Uganda (including Kampala), Nigeria, and an imported case in France.

events.headline: Al-Shabaab Claims Mass-Casualty Ambush on Somali Convoy in Lower Shabelle
events.summary: On Oct 26-27, 2026, al-Shabaab ambushed a Somali government/allied-militia convoy near Leego, Lower Shabelle region, during Operation Banooda, using explosive-laden vehicles; al-Shabaab claims it killed over 300 troops, while Somali officials counter it was a major assault by government forces. The death toll is independently unconfirmed, but analysts call it the army's worst setback since 2023.

events.headline: Russian Bombing of Aid Site and Shelter in Komyshuvakha Kills At Least 26
events.summary: Russian forces bombed a school used as a humanitarian aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, on Nov 2, then struck a shelter where residents had fled with roughly nine more bombs. The death toll rose through the day to at least 26, with dozens still missing; President Zelensky called the attack 'exceptionally horrific' and declared a day of mourning.

events.headline: Mandatory Evacuations in Pagosa Springs, Colorado, as San Juan River Nears Record Crest
events.summary: A second storm wave triggered mandatory evacuations in Archuleta County, Colorado, as the San Juan River rose to 16.8 feet/11,200 cfs — the second-highest stage on record, just below the historic 1911 mark of 17.8 feet. Highway 160 closed, Red Cross shelters opened, and the Colorado National Guard deployed.

events.headline: US to Host Russia-Ukraine Trilateral Talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11
events.summary: US officials Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will lead trilateral talks with Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11, reviving a diplomatic track on post-war security arrangements that had been suspended since February.

events.headline: Federal Judge Rejects DOJ Bid to Segregate About 20,000 'Likely Non-Citizen' California Ballots
events.summary: A federal judge denied a DOJ emergency request to force California to segregate roughly 20,000 ballots the department claims belong to likely non-citizens, two days before the Nov. 3 election, ruling it would "wreak havoc" on the vote. An appeals panel also rejected a similar request.

events.headline: UN Investigation Finds Hallmarks of Genocide in El Fasher One Year After RSF Takeover
events.summary: A UN fact-finding mission concluded that mass killings, gang rapes and deliberate starvation by the RSF in El Fasher, North Darfur, constitute "the hallmarks of genocide." One year after the city's October 2025 capture, North Darfur's governor alleges RSF forces committed 320 gang-rape cases at El Fasher University and 140 mass graves have been identified; Amnesty International's October 2026 follow-up found ongoing unlawful killings, detention, starvation and torture of civilians.

events.headline: US Carries Out Limited Strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island Near Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: The US military conducted limited 'defensive' strikes on targets on Iran's Qeshm Island on Nov 2-3, officials said, aimed at countering Iranian surface-to-air missile systems threatening shipping near the Strait of Hormuz. Officials stressed the action does not represent a resumption of major combat operations.

events.headline: Nearly 6 Million Face Acute Hunger in Haiti Amid Gang Violence and El Nino Drought
events.summary: The UN estimates nearly 5.94 million Haitians face acute food insecurity, a figure projected to rise to 6.35 million by mid-2027, driven by gang violence and El Nino-linked drought. Separately, the UN human rights office reports more than 5,700 people killed or wounded by gang violence between January and mid-September, including over 1,000 rapes and 230 kidnappings.

events.headline: Historic Flash Flooding Triggers Mass Evacuations in Sedona, Arizona
events.summary: A second Pacific storm dumped up to 4 inches of rain across the Southwest on Nov. 1-2, triggering mandatory evacuations in Sedona zones near Oak Creek and prompting water rescues. The same system caused severe flooding in southern Colorado, where Gov. Polis issued a disaster declaration.

events.headline: Palisades Fire Arson Retrial Begins in Los Angeles Federal Court
events.summary: Jury selection began Nov. 2 in the federal retrial of Jonathan Rinderknecht, who is accused of igniting the Palisades Fire. His first trial ended in a hung jury in June 2026.

events.headline: Learjet Crashes Near Greenacres, Florida, Killing All 9 Aboard
events.summary: A Learjet 60 flying from Austin, Texas, to North Eleuthera, Bahamas, crashed near a residential area in Greenacres, Florida, around 12:50 p.m. on Nov. 1, killing all nine people aboard. Gov. Ron DeSantis called the crash "cataclysmic."

events.headline: RSF Drone Strikes Push Sudan's Power Grid Toward Collapse
events.summary: Rapid Support Forces drones have struck 15-18 power stations across Sudan since early October, including the 500-megawatt Um Dabakir plant on Oct 29, cutting White Nile and North Kordofan states off the national grid. The campaign threatens to collapse what remains of Sudan's electricity infrastructure amid the ongoing civil war.

events.headline: Machado Returns From Exile, Presses Rodríguez on Election Timeline
events.summary: María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Oct 25 after more than 10 months in exile and held her first press conference on Oct 29, calling for presidential elections in 2027 and praising the Trump administration. Interim President Delcy Rodríguez said earlier the same day elections would be held "with the world as witness" but gave no firm date.

events.headline: Melania Trump-Brokered Oleshky Ceasefire Expires After Six Days as Russia Declines Extension
events.summary: The six-day localized truce around Oleshky, the longest local pause in fighting since Russia's 2022 invasion, expired Nov 1 after Russia declined Ukraine's offer to extend it. The pause enabled evacuation of nearly 800 civilians with no reported violations; Ukrainian officials now warn fighting could resume worse than before.

events.headline: Haiti Gang Leader Claims Missing Salvadoran Soldiers Killed, Seeks UN Mediation
events.summary: Wilson 'Lanmo Sanjou' Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, wrote to the UN Secretary-General claiming the four Salvadoran soldiers missing since the Oct 18 Croix-des-Bouquets attack were killed by a rival gang, and requested mediation. Haitian and Salvadoran officials say the soldiers may still be alive; the UN confirmed receiving the letter but denies recognizing any mediation role.

events.headline: Bangladesh Measles Outbreak Death Toll Rises to 1,254 as Cases Top 230,000
events.summary: Two more children died of measles-related causes in the 24 hours to Nov 1, bringing Bangladesh's combined suspected-and-confirmed measles death toll since March 15 to 1,254. Cumulative suspected cases nationwide reached 230,013.

events.headline: US Strike Kills Five on Suspected Drug Boat; Cumulative Toll Tops 240
events.summary: On Oct 27, 2026, US forces killed five people in a strike on a boat in the Eastern Pacific, part of the renamed Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere's campaign against alleged drug traffickers, bringing the cumulative death toll to at least 240 across more than 70 strikes since Sept 2025. Family members of victims in at least one earlier strike dispute the "narco-terrorist" characterization.

events.headline: Herzog Opens Coalition Consultations as Eisenkot Positioned to Receive First Mandate
events.summary: President Isaac Herzog began formal coalition-formation consultations in Jerusalem; opposition bloc leader Gadi Eisenkot was positioned to receive the first mandate (28 days, extendable by 14) after securing recommendations from Bennett's B'Yachad, the Joint List and Ra'am, totaling roughly 67 seats. Eisenkot has reiterated he will not form a government with Netanyahu.

events.headline: Third Polish Ambassador Resigns Amid Tusk-Nawrocki Constitutional Court Standoff
events.summary: Poland's UN ambassador Krzysztof Szczerski resigned on Nov 2, the third senior envoy to quit amid an escalating standoff between PM Tusk and President Nawrocki over Constitutional Tribunal judges. Riot police were deployed outside the court as the crisis deepened.

events.headline: North Korea Tests Cluster-Bomb Warhead for Tactical Ballistic Missile
events.summary: On Oct 31, North Korea's Missile Administration test-fired a short-range ballistic missile fitted with a "Standard Type 2" cluster warhead, with state media claiming the munition can turn a 12-13 hectare target area to scorched earth. Pyongyang said it intends to field various cluster-warhead types by end of 2026, amid heightened DMZ tensions including a landmine blast that wounded South Korean soldiers.

events.headline: Minnesota Sues Federal Government Over Withheld Evidence in Fatal ICE Shootings
events.summary: Minnesota sued the Trump administration, DOJ and DHS after federal officials suspended the transfer of evidence needed for state investigations into fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by federal agents during "Operation Metro Surge." The lawsuit seeks access to evidence for the state probes.

events.headline: RBA Raises Cash Rate to 4.85%, Highest Since 2008
events.summary: Australia's central bank raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% on Nov 3 in a 6-3 board vote, the fifth hike of 2026, citing annual inflation at 3.7% and spillover effects from Middle East oil-price volatility.

events.headline: US Measles Cases Hit 4,852 as PAHO Delays Elimination-Status Review
events.summary: CDC data confirm 4,852 US measles cases as of Oct 29, 2026 — the highest since elimination was declared in 2000. PAHO's Regional Verification Commission postponed its review to Nov 10-13, 2026, to allow additional genomic analysis; losing elimination status would reclassify measles in the US from imported to endemic.

events.headline: Displacement From Moyale Ethiopia-Kenya Border Clashes Rises to Nearly 50,000
events.summary: UN agencies report that arrivals into Marsabit County, northern Kenya, fleeing clashes between Oromia and Somali regional forces around Moyale, have risen from roughly 36,000 to nearly 50,000 since the violence began around Oct 22. UN agencies have launched an $8.9 million appeal to support up to 50,000 displaced people.

events.headline: Christa Pike, Who Survived Botched Tennessee Execution, Issues First Public Statement
events.summary: Death-row inmate Christa Pike, who survived a botched lethal injection attempt a month ago at Riverbend prison in Nashville, released her first public statement saying she remains in constant pain. Tennessee executions remain paused pending a review.

events.headline: Rubio Hosts Venezuelan FM Blanco, Reaffirms Three-Phase Transition Plan
events.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Venezuela's new Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco on Nov 2, reaffirming a three-phase stabilization, economic-recovery and democratic-transition plan for Venezuela. Rubio urged the release of political prisoners, with Foro Penal counting 344 currently detained.

events.headline: China's CXMT Completes Validation of Next-Generation 4F2 DRAM Chip
events.summary: Chinese memory maker CXMT completed engineering-sample verification of its sixth-generation 4F2-architecture DRAM chip in early November, targeting DDR5 server modules by year-end. The breakthrough intensifies competition with Samsung and SK Hynix amid a global chip market selloff.

events.headline: South Korea's Kospi Plunges Over 3% as Chip Stocks Tumble on AI Valuation Fears
events.summary: South Korea's Kospi index fell roughly 3-3.6% on Nov 3, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix shares dropping 4.6-5.1%, amid a broader US tech selloff driven by doubts over AI infrastructure spending.

events.headline: France's National Assembly to Vote Nov 3 on 2027 Budget, Risking Collapse of Lecornu Government
events.summary: France's National Assembly is scheduled to vote Nov 3, 2026 on the revenue half of the 2027 budget; 289 votes against would topple PM Sébastien Lecornu's minority government. The Socialist Party, whose abstention kept Lecornu in office through earlier no-confidence votes, is reportedly considering voting him down this time.

events.headline: Overnight Russian Strikes Hit Energy Grid Across Four Ukrainian Oblasts, Killing One
events.summary: Russian missiles and drones struck energy infrastructure overnight Nov 1-2 across Dnipropetrovsk, Khmelnytskyi, Vinnytsia and Zhytomyr oblasts, leaving hundreds of thousands without power; Zhytomyr Oblast alone had at least 650 settlements cut off. Ukrainian authorities reported one killed and at least 47 injured nationwide, with rolling blackouts imposed Nov 2.

events.headline: Israeli Strikes Kill Eight Palestinians in Gaza, Including Five Police Officers and a Child
events.summary: An Israeli drone strike killed five Palestinian police officers on duty in al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis, on Nov 1, 2026. In a separate strike the same day on al-Rimal neighborhood in Gaza City, three Palestinians including a four-year-old child were killed. Gaza's ministry says 75 police/security personnel have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire began.

events.headline: Truck-Bomb and Drone Attack Near Colombian Military Base Kills Four Civilians, Including Infant
events.summary: A truck/cylinder-bomb and drone attack struck near a military base in Planadas, Tolima, on the night of Nov 1-2, killing four civilians including a two-month-old baby and injuring 17. The blast damaged a hospital and homes; no group has claimed responsibility, though FARC dissidents are suspected. Authorities imposed a curfew.

events.headline: Nationwide 'GenZ Regelt' Protests in Germany Turn Violent
events.summary: Tens of thousands protested cost-of-living, education and budget-cut policies across German cities on Oct 31-Nov 1, with clashes in Frankfurt, Berlin, Hamburg and Cologne. Police used water cannon and pepper spray after Molotov cocktails were thrown and shops were looted; officials blamed 'infiltrators' for the violence.

events.headline: Bolivia Declares National State of Emergency Over El Niño Drought
events.summary: President Rodrigo Paz signed a decree Oct 31 declaring a national state of emergency to unlock relief funding amid an intensifying El Niño. Drought is affecting roughly 78,000 families across six departments and has killed more than 75,000 cattle, while authorities also prepare for flood risk as El Niño peaks.

events.headline: Saudi-Led Coalition Strikes Ras Isa Oil Port; Houthis Claim 75 Strikes on Saudi Territory in 24 Hours
events.summary: Houthi media reported Saudi-led coalition airstrikes hit the Ras Isa oil terminal, an oil station in Bajil district, and a telecom facility near Saada city; the coalition confirmed a "precision operation" against Houthi resources. The Houthi spokesman claimed 75 Houthi strikes hit eight Saudi provinces in 24 hours and said the coalition intercepted a Houthi drone and missile.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Airstrikes Kill Children at Karenni School, Bomb Rakhine Villages
events.summary: On Oct 31, a Myanmar military jet bombed a school serving displaced children in Wan Ngao village, Loikaw Township, Karenni State, reportedly killing several students. Separately, around Nov 1, the military dropped bombs on Pauktaw town and Ywar Chaung Gyi village in Rakhine State, injuring civilians including a child and damaging homes.

events.headline: Pakistan Presses Afghan Taliban Over TTP as US Secretary of State Offers Mediation Role
events.summary: On Nov 1, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington would play a "productive role" if asked to mediate, after Russia also offered to mediate between Islamabad and Kabul. The dispute follows recent Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan's Kunar and Helmand provinces that killed up to 22 people by Pakistani count; Islamabad continues to demand the Taliban curb TTP attacks launched from Afghan territory.

events.headline: Thousands Rally in New Delhi Demanding Resignation of India's Election Chief
events.summary: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi led a rally in New Delhi on Nov 1 demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a voter-roll revision that purged more than 130 million names. The opposition alleges the revision disproportionately benefits the ruling BJP.

events.headline: PAHO Warns of Dengue and Chikungunya Resurgence Across the Americas
events.summary: The Pan American Health Organization reports 1.69 million suspected dengue cases across the Americas as of mid-September 2026, including 3,413 severe cases and 571 deaths. Chikungunya is also resurging in Guyana, French Guiana, Suriname and Paraguay, prompting a US CDC health advisory.

events.headline: UN Peacekeeping Mission in Western Sahara Ends After 35 Years
events.summary: The UN Security Council failed to renew the mandate of MINURSO, its peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, triggering a wind-down that began Nov 1 after 35 years of operation.

events.headline: Niger Receives First Algerian Fuel Convoy Under Joint Military Escort
events.summary: Around 53-60 Algerian fuel trucks carrying roughly 1.65 million liters arrived in Agadez, Niger, on Oct 31-Nov 1 under joint military escort, marking Algeria's first troop deployment abroad since 1973.

events.headline: South Africa Holds Nationwide Local Government Elections
events.summary: South Africans vote Nov 4 in local government elections for 10,526 council seats, with special voting held Nov 2-3 and 732 parties registered to contest seats nationwide.

events.headline: Prescott, Arizona Declares State of Emergency After Flooding Overtops Watson Lake Dam
events.summary: Prescott's mayor declared a state of emergency after heavy rainfall overtopped the Watson Lake (Granite) Dam, with inflow peaking above 4,000 cfs; the Upper Goldwater Reservoir also topped. The dam is rated to safely handle up to 10 feet of overtopping; low-water crossings closed.

events.headline: One Year After Typhoon Halong, Kipnuk and Kwigillingok Villages Remain in Limbo Amid FEMA Relocation Dispute
events.summary: A year after the remnants of Typhoon Halong destroyed over 150 homes and forced roughly 1,500 evacuations in the Yup'ik villages of Kipnuk and Kwigillingok, Alaska, most residents remain displaced. Both villages voted to relocate entirely, but the state's FEMA request to fund permanent replacement housing for 219 damaged homes has been denied, and temporary housing assistance is set to expire in April 2027.

events.headline: Georgia Ponzi Scheme Founder Brant Frost Sentenced to 15 Years, Ordered to Pay $76.4 Million Restitution
events.summary: Edwin Brant Frost IV, founder of First Liberty Building & Loan in Newnan, Georgia, was sentenced to 15 years in prison and ordered to pay $76.4 million in restitution after pleading guilty to wire fraud in a Ponzi scheme the SEC says defrauded roughly 300 investors of about $140 million. Funds were also funneled to conservative political causes and Alabama politicians.

events.headline: Lawsuit Could Strip Medicaid Coverage From 140,000 Ohioans
events.summary: The American Medical Association filed an amicus brief backing a lawsuit brought by the City of Columbus challenging a federal Medicaid work-requirement rule. The AMA warned the rule could cause up to 140,000 Ohio Medicaid-expansion enrollees to lose coverage.

events.headline: UN Envoy Says Sudan-RSF Transition Talks Expected Before Christmas
events.summary: UN special envoy for Sudan Pekka Haavisto told reporters talks with the RSF on a transition to civilian rule are expected "before Christmas," saying there is "no military solution" to the conflict. The Quintet (UN, EU, AU, Arab League, IGAD) continues to push a peace track.

events.headline: Ohio Measles Outbreak Expands to 24 Counties, Cases Nearly 600% Higher Than 2025
events.summary: Ohio has recorded 296 measles cases across 24 counties in 2026 — a roughly 558-600% increase over 2025's 45 cases — in the state's third distinct outbreak of the year, concentrated in Wayne, Geauga, Ashtabula and Medina counties. Officials cite MMR vaccination coverage (88.3%) below the 95% herd-immunity threshold.

events.headline: Brigham and Women's Hospital Nurses Set Open-Ended Strike for Nov. 12 Amid Contract Fight
events.summary: More than 4,000 Brigham and Women's Hospital nurses issued a 10-day notice for an open-ended strike starting Nov. 12 after rejecting Mass General Brigham's "last, best, final" contract offer. Talks resume Nov. 9, three days before the deadline; disputes center on pay, staffing ratios, and insurance choice.

events.headline: Mayor Mamdani Threatens Legal Action Against ICE Over Use of NYC Park Lots as Staging Grounds
events.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani sent DHS a letter demanding ICE stop using city-owned lots at Van Cortlandt Park (Bronx) and near Flushing Meadows Corona Park (Queens) as enforcement staging areas, calling it unauthorized under his February executive order, and threatening legal action.

events.headline: Widespread Flooding Prompts State of Emergency, School Closures in Okeechobee and Brevard Counties, Florida
events.summary: A slow-moving storm dumped 5-10 inches of rain across Florida Nov. 1-2, flooding roads in Okeechobee County (which declared a state of emergency) and Brevard County (Palm Bay, Titusville, Satellite Beach, Cocoa Beach). Schools in both counties plus Florida Tech closed Monday.

events.headline: Two Teenagers Killed in Halloween-Night Shooting Outside Spartanburg Cook Out
events.summary: A 15-year-old (Jayden Watkins) and a 17-year-old (Shane Dawkins) were shot and killed around 11:30 p.m. Oct. 31 in the parking lot of a Cook Out restaurant in Spartanburg, South Carolina. A third person suffered non-life-threatening injuries; no suspects had been identified as of Nov. 2.

events.headline: Fatal Shooting at Madison Senior High School Youth Football Game in Illinois
events.summary: One adult was killed and three others wounded in a shooting shortly after 10:45 p.m. Nov. 1 at Madison Senior High School in Madison, Illinois (St. Louis metro area) during a youth football league championship game. The school canceled classes Monday and Tuesday, and the Major Case Squad of Greater St. Louis is investigating.

events.headline: Halloween-Weekend Violence Leaves 3 Dead, About 11 Injured Across Philadelphia
events.summary: A wave of 11 separate shootings and stabbings over Halloween weekend in Philadelphia killed three people, including a 15-year-old, and injured roughly 11 others. Police are investigating the incidents, which occurred across multiple neighborhoods.

events.headline: Oklahoma Officials Seek Dismissal of Lawsuit Challenging State's Near-Total Abortion Ban
events.summary: Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond filed a motion to dismiss a Center for Reproductive Rights lawsuit brought by three women who were denied abortions despite fatal fetal diagnoses. The case challenges the state's near-total abortion ban.

events.headline: Daimler Truck Shutters Nearly 80-Year-Old Portland Manufacturing Plant, Cutting About 375 Jobs
events.summary: Daimler Truck North America closed its Swan Island plant in Portland, Oregon, on Oct. 30, cutting roughly 375 to 387 jobs. The closure ends 84 years of Freightliner-legacy manufacturing in Portland as production shifts to North and South Carolina.

events.headline: Trump Says Flávio Bolsonaro Can Stay in US Indefinitely
events.summary: On Oct 31, President Trump said Flávio Bolsonaro, who fled Brazil for the US after his election loss and a passport-revocation order, "can stay here as long as he wants," and called Brazil's election "a disgrace" despite international observers deeming it free and fair.

events.headline: Eurozone Inflation Hits Three-Year High of 3.8%; ECB Delivers Hawkish Hold
events.summary: Eurostat confirmed euro-area annual inflation rose to 3.8% in September 2026 (from 3.2%), its highest since 2023, driven by an 18.9% jump in energy prices. At its Oct 29 meeting the ECB kept rates unchanged (deposit rate 2.50%), a "hawkish hold" with markets pricing a chance of a December hike.

events.headline: Swiss Foreign Minister Visits Pyongyang, First Such Visit Since 2003, as Diplomatic Office Reopens
events.summary: Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis traveled to Pyongyang Oct 29-30 to reopen Switzerland's diplomatic office and held talks with North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui. The two sides discussed regularizing political relations; it is the first visit by a Swiss foreign minister to North Korea since 2003.

events.headline: Australia Faces Sharpest Property Downturn in 40 Years as Trust in Politicians Falls
events.summary: National house prices fell for a seventh consecutive month through October, with capital-city values down 8.1% over seven months — the fastest decline in 40 years. Separately, the 2026 McKinnon Index found trust in federal politicians fell from 35.9% to 30.5% over the past year, with support for democracy among young men dropping notably.

events.headline: Jordan Intercepts 14 Armed Individuals Crossing From Syria
events.summary: Jordanian forces stopped a group of 14 armed individuals attempting to cross from Syria into Mafraq Governorate on Oct 30-31, exchanging fire that killed some while others fled back across the border. The incident follows earlier Jordanian strikes on Syria after a deadly church attack in Jordan.

events.headline: Severe Storms, Tornado Threat Strike Northwest Missouri and Northeast Kansas
events.summary: A Level 2-of-5 "Slight Risk" severe weather outlook covered the Kansas City, St. Joseph and Topeka region on Nov. 2, with damaging winds and isolated tornadoes cited as the primary threats. Forecasters warned residents to monitor conditions through the evening.

events.headline: France Releases Strategic Diesel Reserves; Retailers Cut Pump Prices
events.summary: France began releasing roughly 10 million barrels (about 20% of its strategic diesel stockpile) from Nov 1, 2026, in a move expected to cut pump prices by 12-18 centimes per litre. Major retailers announced cuts of up to 21 centimes/litre at their stations.

events.headline: Anthrax Outbreak Kills Nearly 30 Hippos in DR Congo's Virunga National Park
events.summary: Bacillus anthracis has killed approximately 28-30 hippos along the Semuliki River in Virunga National Park over the past month, prompting zoonotic-risk warnings for nearby communities.

events.headline: Antonio Navarro Wolff, Co-Author of Colombia's 1991 Constitution, Dies at 78
events.summary: Antonio Navarro Wolff, former M-19 guerrilla commander who later became a mainstream politician, co-president of Colombia's 1991 Constituent Assembly, senator, and governor of Nariño, died Nov 1, 2026, at age 78. He was a longtime ally of Gustavo Petro.

events.headline: Federal Agents Take Over Arson Probe at Senatobia, Mississippi, Police Headquarters
events.summary: The ATF took over the investigation into suspected arson that damaged the Senatobia, Mississippi, police department building on Oct. 31. The department has faced prior controversy after an officer fatally shot a 1-year-old child in June and the chief was fired over racist texts.

events.headline: Incumbent Iliana Iotova Wins Bulgaria's Presidential Runoff, First Woman Directly Elected President
events.summary: Acting President Iliana Iotova won Bulgaria's Nov 1 presidential runoff against former caretaker PM Andrey Gyurov, becoming Bulgaria's first woman directly elected to the presidency. Her opponent conceded; analysts note the result consolidates influence for PM Rumen Radev, seen as Ukraine-skeptic.

events.headline: Mayor Mamdani Says Trump Will Grant Visa to Mother of Bronx Shooting Victim
events.summary: New York City Mayor Mamdani said President Trump agreed to expedite a visa for the mother of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong, who was fatally shot in the Bronx. Three teenage suspects in the shooting remain at large.

events.headline: Serbia Marks Second Anniversary of Novi Sad Canopy Collapse Amid Political Transition
events.summary: Thousands marched in Novi Sad on Nov 1 and held 16 minutes of silence for the 16 victims of the 2024 railway station canopy collapse, a week after the Students' List movement won parliamentary elections over President Vucic's SNS party. Thirteen officials, including a former minister, remain under prosecution.

events.headline: Formal Complaint Filed Against Ex-President Petro Over Election-Fraud Claims
events.summary: On Oct 27, 2026, lawyer Jaime Lombana, backed by the Conservative Party, filed a complaint against former President Gustavo Petro before Colombia's Accusation Commission, alleging Petro disrupted the democratic process and promoted unsubstantiated fraud claims after losing the 2026 election to Abelardo De La Espriella.

events.headline: Egypt's Central Bank Raises Key Rate to 20%; IMF Lifts 2026 Growth Forecast to 5.1%
events.summary: The Central Bank of Egypt raised its overnight deposit rate by 100 basis points to 20% — its first hike since March 2024 — citing risks from global energy/commodity prices and domestic fiscal consolidation. The IMF separately raised its 2026 Egypt GDP growth forecast to 5.1% (from 4.2%), while flagging persistent inflation (~14.5%) and debt/currency risks.

events.headline: Anti-Robotaxi Group Becomes D.C.'s Top Political Ad Spender, Outspending Mayoral Candidates
events.summary: The Coalition for Accountability and Road Safety has spent over $2.6 million opposing a D.C. Council bill that would legalize commercial robotaxis — more than either leading mayoral candidate — per a Washington Post analysis of AdImpact data.

events.headline: Peru's Annual Inflation Hits 5.25%, Highest Since 2023
events.summary: Peru's annual inflation rate rose to 5.25% in October 2026, up from 4.55% in September, marking the eighth consecutive month above the central bank's 1-3% target range. Rising fuel and food prices, exacerbated by El Nino conditions, are driving the increase.

events.headline: Russia Formally Withdraws From Council of Europe Anti-Torture Convention
events.summary: Russia's withdrawal from the European Convention for the Prevention of Torture took effect Nov 1, ending independent monitoring of Russian detention facilities by the Council of Europe's CPT committee.

events.headline: Gabon's President Oligui Nguema Begins State Visit to China
events.summary: Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema began a state visit to China on Nov 3 at President Xi Jinping's invitation, running through Nov 7. Afreximbank separately forecasts Gabon's 2026 GDP growth accelerating to 3.3%.

events.headline: Comcast Slashes 634 Jobs at Philadelphia Headquarters, Citing AI Investment
events.summary: Comcast filed a WARN notice confirming 634 layoffs at its Philadelphia headquarters effective Dec. 31 as part of an AI-driven customer-service restructuring. The company also filed notices for cuts in New Jersey, Washington and California, while planning more than 1,100 new hires companywide.

events.headline: Ecuador Imposes Fourth Coastal Curfew of 2026 Ahead of Nov 29 Local Elections
events.summary: Ecuador's government imposed its fourth curfew of the year across five coastal provinces (Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro, Esmeraldas) from Nov 1-10, resulting in 218 arrests, ahead of Nov 29 local elections. The move follows the Oct 22 arrest of opposition leader Luisa Gonzalez on campaign-finance allegations, which her party calls politically motivated.

events.headline: Cockeysville, Maryland, Man Shoots Three Masked Men on His Property on Halloween, Killing One
events.summary: A homeowner in Cockeysville, Maryland, opened fire on three masked, allegedly armed men who approached him on Halloween night, killing 20-year-old Amon Walker and wounding two others. Baltimore County Police are investigating the shooting.

events.headline: Lebanese Delegation Holds Talks With Syria on Refugees and Border Security
events.summary: A Lebanese ministerial delegation led by Deputy PM Tarek Mitri met Syrian Foreign Minister al-Shaibani in Damascus on Nov 2, discussing refugee returns, border security, prisoners and anti-trafficking cooperation.

events.headline: Texas Amazon Delivery Contractors and Food Processor File WARN Notices, Cutting About 400 Jobs
events.summary: 4XH Logistics, a Boerne-based Amazon delivery contractor, is laying off 230 workers in the San Antonio area (Nov. 6-19) after its Amazon contract expired. Eagles Delivery LLC separately cut 115 jobs after shuttering its Roanoke, TX facility; CTI Foods Bean LLC is closing its Saginaw, TX plant, eliminating 66 jobs effective Nov. 9.

events.headline: Argentina's Country-Risk Index Surpasses 800 Points, Highest in Over a Year
events.summary: JP Morgan's EMBI country-risk index for Argentina closed at 803 points on Nov 2, having touched 805 intraday, its highest level in more than a year. The spike reflects investor concerns over reserves, debt sustainability and financing conditions.

events.headline: Poland Deploys Counter-Terrorism Police to Kaliningrad Border Over Sabotage Warnings
events.summary: Poland launched a counter-terrorism operation along its border with Russia's Kaliningrad exclave, running Nov 2-8, deploying special police units, military and intelligence services after warnings of possible armed crossings from Russia.

events.headline: Italy Issues Orange Alert for Storms and Flash Flooding in Puglia and Basilicata
events.summary: Italy's Civil Protection department issued an orange weather alert for Puglia and Basilicata on Nov 2-3 due to intense thunderstorms and flash-flood risk linked to a weak polar vortex, with yellow alerts issued in five other regions.

events.headline: Greek PM Mitsotakis Unveils 90-Project Reform Plan Ahead of 2027 Election
events.summary: Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announced a plan of 90 infrastructure, defence, housing and public-service projects, with 26 due by the end of 2026 and 64 by mid-2027, ahead of Greece's spring 2027 election.

events.headline: 36-Hour Shutdown Paralyzes Upper Siang Over Mega Dam Project in Arunachal Pradesh
events.summary: A 36-hour bandh began Nov 2 in Yingkiong, Upper Siang district, disrupting schools, markets and transport, with mobile internet suspended. Protesters are demanding the release of detained activists and a halt to survey work for the proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper hydropower project; the state chief minister has pledged dialogue.

events.headline: Fiji Delays Vote on Constitution Amendment Bill to December
events.summary: Fiji's PM Sitiveni Rabuka announced the Special Parliamentary Committee's review of the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 would be delayed to Nov 30, pushing the final vote to early December, after opposition and coalition-partner concerns over a rushed timetable.

events.headline: Deadly Flooding and Landslides Hit Santa Cruz Island, Galápagos
events.summary: Heavy El Niño-driven rainfall caused flooding and landslides on Santa Cruz Island, killing one person, leaving two missing, and prompting evacuation of about 80 residents; roughly 2,000 families were affected and the Baltra Island airport suspended commercial flights.

events.headline: RPG Shell Kills Two at Sebha Marble Factory; Armed Group Shuts Key Libyan Oil Pipeline Valve
events.summary: An old RPG shell detonated at a marble factory in Sebha's Hijara area on Oct 30, 2026, killing two workers and injuring a third during demolition work. Separately, Libya's National Oil Corporation confirmed an armed group forcibly closed the main valve on the Hamada crude pipeline feeding the Zawiya refinery around Oct 31, halting roughly 15,000 barrels/day of crude flow.

events.headline: South Korea's President Lee Unveils Record 820.9 Trillion Won Budget Amid Opposition Pushback
events.summary: President Lee Jae-myung delivered his 2027 Budget Address on Nov 2, proposing a record 820.9 trillion won ($610B) spending plan — a 12.8% increase, the fastest annual rise in South Korean history — including nearly doubled AI/semiconductor investment and an 8.2% defense increase. The budget faces opposition from the People Power Party.

events.headline: FBI Probes Former Burlington, Vermont School Administrator Over Alleged $1.8 Million Fraud
events.summary: Federal investigators are examining whether former Burlington School District administrator Stephanie Phillips defrauded the district of at least $1.77 million since 2013 by billing through a fake consulting company while drawing her regular salary. No criminal charges filed yet; she retired in May.

events.headline: Rockslide Shuts Down Lehigh Gorge Scenic Railway Indefinitely in the Poconos
events.summary: A rockslide on Route 209 between Jim Thorpe and Nesquehoning, PA on Oct. 31 damaged the roadway and tracks, forcing the Reading & Northern's Lehigh Gorge Scenic Railway to suspend all excursions indefinitely. Route 209 closed in both directions with a 6-8 week reopening estimate.

events.headline: Authors, 'Read Freely Alabama' Sue State Library Board Over Transgender-Themed Book Ban
events.summary: Read Freely Alabama and three authors filed a federal lawsuit against the Alabama Public Library Service over a rule barring youth library books referencing transgender people, alleging First Amendment violations and financial harm to authors.

events.headline: Washington Supreme Court Rejects Seattle's Appeal in Public-Records Case Brought by Podcaster Brandi Kruse
events.summary: The Washington State Supreme Court declined to hear Seattle's appeal of a lower ruling that found the city violated the Public Records Act in a suit brought by podcaster Brandi Kruse over records tied to a 2023 city council vote. The court also awarded attorney fees to the Citizen Action Defense Fund, which represented Kruse.

events.headline: Washington Court of Appeals Revives Landlord's Takings Lawsuit Against Seattle Rental Regulations
events.summary: Washington's Court of Appeals, Division One, reversed a King County Superior Court dismissal and ruled Goodman Real Estate's lawsuit over the Addison on Fourth apartments — alleging a "regulatory taking" from Seattle tenant-protection laws passed 2018-2021 — can proceed. The 254-unit complex's rent collections reportedly fell from 94% to 44% and it is now in receivership.

events.headline: Bird Flu Detected at Colorado Dairy for First Time Since 2024
events.summary: Colorado's state veterinary lab confirmed highly pathogenic avian influenza in a Weld County dairy herd on Oct. 24, the first detection in a Colorado dairy since the 2024 outbreak. The facility is under quarantine, and officials say pasteurized milk remains safe.

events.headline: Honolulu City Council Members Face Sunshine Law Probe Over Secret Zippy's Meeting
events.summary: Five of nine Honolulu City Council members, a quorum, are under a state Office of Information Practices investigation after complaints alleged they privately discussed leadership and committee assignments at a Zippy's restaurant. Such a gathering could violate Hawaii's open-meetings Sunshine law.

events.headline: Anchorage Faces Looming 'Fiscal Cliff' as Mayor Proposes Flat $692.5 Million 2027 Budget
events.summary: Anchorage Mayor Suzanne LaFrance proposed a $692.5 million flat FY2027 municipal budget that closes a roughly $15 million gap using one-time funds. Officials warned the shortfall could nearly double to about $30 million in 2028.

events.headline: Taiwan Accuses China of Harassment After Coast Guard Standoff Near Pratas Islands
events.summary: A Chinese coast guard vessel entered restricted waters near Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands on Nov 1, coming within roughly 1 nautical mile of a Taiwanese coast guard ship that confronted and expelled it. Taiwan's coast guard said this was the 13th such Chinese intrusion near the islands in 2026.

events.headline: String of Indiana Factory Closures Cuts Hundreds of Jobs
events.summary: Three Indiana plants are closing in late 2026: ZF Active Safety & Electronics will shut its Lafayette steering-components plant Nov. 30 (133 jobs); Packaging Corporation of America is closing its Gas City containerboard plant (72 jobs); and PMG Indiana is winding down its 39-year-old Columbus auto-parts plant (about 150 jobs by year-end).

events.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory Hits San Francisco Bay Area as Pacific Storm Brings High Tides, Beach Hazards
events.summary: A "Pineapple Express" atmospheric-river storm triggered a coastal flood advisory for San Francisco, Monterey Bay, and the Big Sur coast, with up to 1.5 feet of inundation possible in low-lying shoreline areas and elevated risk of sneaker waves and rip currents through Tuesday evening.

events.headline: Massachusetts Gun Owners Hit New Firearm Registration Deadline Days Before Vote on Question 9
events.summary: An Oct. 28 deadline passed requiring Massachusetts gun owners to register and serialize previously grandfathered firearms under the state's 2024 gun law. The deadline came six days ahead of the Nov. 3 ballot vote on Question 9, which would affect the registry law.

events.headline: Four Iowa Nursing Homes Cited for Alleged Resident Abuse or Injuries, One Death
events.summary: Iowa state inspectors cited four nursing homes for alleged resident injuries or abuse. The most serious case involved a resident at Azria Health Prairie Ridge in Mediapolis who died after receiving an opioid overdose roughly ten times the prescribed amount.

events.headline: ECDC Reports Early Flu Season Driven by H3N2 Subclade K Alongside West Nile Activity in Europe
events.summary: ECDC's weekly communicable disease threat reports show influenza A(H3N2) subclade K is the dominant circulating strain, prompting a threat-assessment brief, though overall EU/EEA flu/RSV circulation remained low in early Oct while SARS-CoV-2 was increasing. ECDC also recorded West Nile virus activity across 18 countries and chikungunya cases in two European countries, plus isolated measles cases in Serbia.

events.headline: Fire Forces Evacuation of Jamaica Plain Apartment Building in Boston, 12+ Displaced
events.summary: A fire at a six-unit building at 211 Boylston St. in Boston's Jamaica Plain neighborhood on Oct. 31 caused the rear wall to become structurally unstable, displacing more than 12 residents. No injuries were reported.
